WITH aretes AS (...), c(dest, chemin, t) AS (SELECT dest, CAST(src + ' > ' + dest AS NVARCHAR(4000)), t FROM aretes WHERE src = 'PC-COMPTA-07' UNION ALL SELECT e.dest, CAST(c.chemin + ' > ' + e.dest AS NVARCHAR(4000)), e.t FROM c JOIN aretes e ON e.src = c.dest AND e.t > c.t AND CHARINDEX(e.dest, c.chemin) = 0) SELECT chemin, t AS arrivee FROM c WHERE dest = 'DC01'
35.5.note: Une CTE ordinaire et une CTE récursive se mélangent dans le même WITH ; le chemin, qui s'allonge, doit être typé NVARCHAR(4000) des deux côtés.

require.msg: Calcule les intervalles avec LAG.

hints: Intervalles : CAST(DATEDIFF(second, LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage), horodatage) AS FLOAT). SQL Server a une fonction d'écart type de population : STDEVP.

WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, CAST(DATEDIFF(second, LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage), horodatage) AS FLOAT) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, STDEVP(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50) SELECT host, domaine, n AS intervalles, ROUND(m, 0) AS moyenne_s, ... ORDER BY cv, host
36.3.note: STDEVP remplace sqrt(AVG(x*x) - AVG(x)*AVG(x)). Le CAST en FLOAT évite une moyenne entière (DATEDIFF renvoie un INT), et ROUND exige son 2e argument.

36.4.solution: WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, CAST(DATEDIFF(second, LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage), horodatage) AS FLOAT) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, STDEVP(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50) SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, ROUND(m, 0) AS moyenne_s FROM st WHERE sd / m < 0.05 AND domaine NOT IN (SELECT domaine FROM domaines_connus);

36.5.solution: WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, CAST(DATEDIFF(second, LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage), horodatage) AS FLOAT) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, STDEVP(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT domaine FROM st WHERE sd / m < 0.05 AND domaine NOT IN (SELECT domaine FROM domaines_connus)), h AS (SELECT DISTINCT domaine, ip_dest, host FROM proxy_logs WHERE domaine IN (SELECT domaine FROM b)), l AS (SELECT domaine, ip_dest, STRING_AGG(host, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY host) AS machines FROM h GROUP BY domaine, ip_dest) SELECT p.domaine, p.ip_dest, l.machines, MIN(p.horodatage) AS premier, COUNT(*) AS connexions, SUM(p.octets_out) AS octets_envoyes FROM proxy_logs p JOIN l ON l.domaine = p.domaine AND l.ip_dest = p.ip_dest GROUP BY p.domaine, p.ip_dest, l.machines;

require.msg: Concatène les valeurs avec STRING_AGG (l'équivalent de group_concat en SQL Server).

hints: Après les CTE de détection, dédoublonne (domaine, ip_dest, host) puis fais STRING_AGG(host, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY host) : STRING_AGG n'accepte pas DISTINCT.

WITH iv AS (...), st AS (...), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT domaine FROM st WHERE ...), h AS (SELECT DISTINCT domaine, ip_dest, host FROM proxy_logs WHERE domaine IN (SELECT domaine FROM b)), l AS (SELECT domaine, ip_dest, STRING_AGG(host, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY host) AS machines FROM h GROUP BY domaine, ip_dest) SELECT p.domaine, p.ip_dest, l.machines, MIN(p.horodatage) AS premier, ... FROM proxy_logs p JOIN l ... GROUP BY p.domaine, p.ip_dest, l.machines
